MEASURED LIVE against the real 775: design 1 draws 8x8 over a 216-texel square and 32 of the 64 cells — exactly half — have a centre resolving to NO sector; 47.2% of the square's texels resolve to nothing; the dead cells are a complete RING (whole top row, whole bottom row, both side columns, plus the next ring's corners). The defect is AFFORDANCE, not function — pickSector already returns null out there correctly. ⚠ Design 2 is NOT this fix: it has no cell grid at GALAXY and fails the opposite way, cropping 20 of 775 sectors off the glass.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: ⭐ MAX RULED 2026-09-07, shown the A/B: *"I want the nav screen to reflect the actual orientation of the planets in the game, so if B is correct then that's what we use."* B STAYS. And his words set a HIGHER bar than the A/B asked about: not merely 'a real angle once', but the planets' ACTUAL ORIENTATION IN THE GAME. Background: d2System placed bodies at `a = i * 1.7 + 0.6` where `i` is the DRAW-LOOP INDEX, and state.js re-sorts D.bodies on [ / ], so the sort key teleported every planet around its ring. The angle exists upstream (StarSystemGenerator.js:550/609, SolarSystemData.js:723/846) and the LEGACY orrery already reads it (NavComputer.js:2853); buildBodies never copied it across. ⚠ OPEN SUB-QUESTION HIS RULING CREATES: the game ADVANCES orbitAngle every tick (main.js:3145, `entry.orbitAngle += entry.orbitSpeed * celestialDt`), and there is a pin/thaw mechanism at :3216. The nav is handed the live `system._systemData` (main.js:5781), so the plumbing is right — but a 4-second live sample showed the nav's angles STATIC. Either the planet objects are a snapshot, or orbits are pinned in ORRERY. Must be settled by measurement: does the nav's mark sit where the planet actually is RIGHT NOW?

verifyVia.input: At SYSTEM in design 2, watch a fast inner planet over time, and separately press [ and ] to cycle the sort key.
verifyVia.observable: The nav's mark sits where that planet actually is in the game at that moment, and keeps tracking it as it orbits. Every body stays on its own ring across every sort.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: ✅ Real angles built and live; ▶ MAX RULED FOR B. ⚠ NOT YET CLOSED: his 'actual orientation' bar needs the live-tracking question answered. Measured 2026-09-07: nav angles static over 4s and D.bodies faithfully mirrored them, so the adapter is honest — but whether its SOURCE tracks the rendered planet is unsettled. ⚠ ALSO OPEN: B clusters Sol's inner planets so numerals II/III/IV/VI/VII overlap where A's are clean. placeLabel tries 7 vertical offsets against other labels only and cannot solve an angular cluster; unreadable numerals are a defect, not a polish item, so the placer needs a pass.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: FOUND IN PASSING, and it is a live MIS-SELECTION, not an inert region: placeLabel (lab:296-306) walks 7 vertical offsets up to 18 texels from the star it labels and checks each candidate slot only against OTHER ALREADY-PLACED LABELS — never against star dots. So a label can land squarely on an unrelated star's mark, and clicking it selects the wrong star. The prism's index tags have the same drift at a fixed +3,-6 offset, over a field of up to 240 marks with a 3-texel hit radius.

verifyVia.input: At PRISM in design 2, find a placed star label that has drifted away from its own mark, and click the label.
verifyVia.observable: The star the label NAMES is selected — not whatever mark happens to lie under the label's plate. S.labelHits is tested before S.prismHits, so the plate's texels belong to the label's own object.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: FOUND BY THE NEW MARK GUARD, and nothing else could have seen it: design 2's moon pips are a SCREEN-SPACE strip drawn at `x + 4 + m*2, y - 4` (d2System:1416), so a moon-rich planet sitting on an outer orbit near cos(a) ~ 1 runs the strip off the right edge of the map. It was silently CLIPPED before, because rect/sprite/dottedEllipse were unguarded — assertFits is reached only through T() and therefore plated(). Zero firings at the default tilt, which is exactly why no suite is red today; 30 firings across a 1200-frame rotation sweep. The pips are correct as a screen-space badge and must stay one — the fix is to place the strip on whichever side of the body has room, not to tilt it into an ellipse.

verifyVia.input: Sweep the orrery through its full rotation range on a system with a moon-rich outer planet (the lab's own Q/E and arrow keys drive it).
verifyVia.observable: assertMark reports zero overflows at every angle, and the moon pips stay on the glass rather than being clipped at the pane edge.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: ✅ 2,880-frame sweep across both designs and all five levels: ZERO guard firings, against the old budget's overflows at the same angles, with a sabotage control proving the violation channel is live so the zero is not a dead wire. At the default tilt old and new both compute 205.50 — the picture cannot move.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: ⭐ MAX'S BAR ON AC-13, AND IT WAS NOT MET BY THE REAL ANGLE ALONE: *"I want the nav screen to reflect the actual orientation of the planets in the game."* Planets MOVE. main.js:7875 copies orbitAngle into the scene entry as a NUMBER, and from then on the sim advances only the copy (:11358, `entry.orbitAngle += entry.orbitSpeed * celestialDt`). The nav is handed system._systemData — the raw generation data, and main.js:7950's own comment says so — so reading p.orbitAngle draws every planet WHERE IT STARTED, forever. ⛔ AND buildBodies RUNS ONCE PER SYSTEM (generating ~39 names is not cheap), so reading the live value inside it is not enough on its own: the row must be re-read every frame. Both halves are required. Fixed by a `_live` back-reference folded onto main.js:7878 (line count still 15161) plus a per-frame angle refresh in state.js that leaves the cached names alone.

verifyVia.input: At SYSTEM in design 2, watch a fast inner planet for several seconds while the game runs.
verifyVia.observable: Its mark travels around its ring, staying where the planet actually is. Pinned by a test that moves the live angle between two renders WITHOUT changing the system object, so the cache is exercised; both halves mutation-proved — disabling the per-frame refresh fails with 'the orrery froze', ignoring _live fails with 'read the frozen generation angle'.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: ◐ BUILT AND MUTATION-PROVED HEADLESSLY 2026-09-07; ⛔ LIVE CONFIRMATION STILL OPEN, AND THE ATTEMPT FOUND SOMETHING. Driving the running game: nav._systemData.planets[0]._live was UNDEFINED, and window._systemData (main.js:7588) was undefined too — meaning spawnSystem HAD NEVER RUN. In the ORRERY boot state the ship is in deep space with no system spawned, nav._currentSystemData is null, and NavComputer.js:2458 falls through to resolveArrivalSystem — so the SYSTEM screen is drawing a system the nav GENERATED FOR ITSELF, not a spawned one. ⭐ Which means 'the actual orientation of the planets in the game' has no referent in that state: there are no in-game planets yet. The _live wiring is correct and is the right fix for when a system IS spawned; it simply cannot be exercised until one is. ▶ NEXT: select a body, commit the BURN/WARP, and re-run the 6-second sample with the system actually spawned. ⚠ Do NOT mark this green on the headless proof alone — the whole workstream opened on a green test that pinned nothing.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: FOUND IN PASSING AND IT IS THE WORST FAILURE MODE THIS SURFACE HAS: d1Rail dereferences D.playerSector.name unguarded, and state.js can legitimately hand a null playerSector — getSectorAt returns null for any point past R > GALAXY_RADIUS * 1.2 = 18, so a player out there freezes the nav. ⛔ It does not throw visibly: PanelHost catches a painter throw ONCE and then stops uploading, so the glass keeps showing the last good frame and LOOKS ALIVE. A dead screen that looks fine is worse than a crash.

verifyVia.observable: Every painter completes, the glass keeps updating, and no field a design reads is left without a default in state.js.

inputs: nav-240p-lab.html — THE SPEC. Every design change goes here and is re-extracted; designs.js is GENERATED and must never be hand-edited.

src/ui/NavComputer.js — the host. LINE-COUNT-FROZEN at 4711; ~700 line-anchored citations ride it, so new statements FOLD onto existing lines and every comment on a folded line must be /* */ terminated. Lines 586, 4345, 4420 and 4442 end in // and are poisoned. The keyboard fold line is 349.

NavComputer's live drag state — _dragging, _dragStartX/Y, _dragStartRotX/Y, _localRotX/_localRotY (PRISM), _systemRotX/_systemRotY (SYSTEM). All already written at 0.008 rad/px on drag; the designs simply never read them.
src/ui/navViewModes/state.js — the adapter that builds S and D. S.cam and S.view are the pipes the camera and the 2D frame already travel down; rotation is one more field on S.cam.
src/ui/navViewModes/index.js — the driver: modes, buffer, the render-tail hover picker, the keyboard methods, remapClick.
src/ui/navViewModes/picking.js — hit-testing over what the paint published; branches on S.mapProj.kind in exactly one place.
src/generation/NameGenerator.js — generatePlanetName / generateMoonName, whose rng contract state.js does not currently satisfy (AC-10).
outputs: The two 240p nav view modes ('rail' and 'bars') as the player drives them — both ship, per Max's 'I like both versions... let's keep both'.
S.cam gains rotX/rotY; d2System gains a real camera; new published-geometry fields on S for every element AC-2 makes pickable and for the AC-5 click-highlight.

The diegetic cockpit nav panel eventually represents these designs — ⛔ but it MUST NOT change here. Two NavComputer instances exist (main.js:4700 and :5895); the gate is activate(), which _openCockpitNav never calls. NOT _bare, which is permanently false on the panel.
mustStayWorking: node scripts/extract-nav-designs.mjs --check exits 0 — designs.js matches the lab.
viewMode === null is today's nav, byte for byte.

Suites at baseline: tests/ 20 failed across the same 8 files (agent-camera-api, driver-pack-giantdeck, gas-body-lab-material, lab-shader-perframe-seam, moon-condition-contract, moon-rng-stream-identity, port-condition-contract, relief-octave-lod-ramp); src/cockpit 698 passed; src/ui 520 passed (baseline moved 480 -> 520 when the three build agents landed 40 new tests). ⚠ navViewModes.test.js's 'rail: every level tab changes level when clicked where it is drawn' failed once under a full src/ui run and passed 3/3 in isolation — cross-test pollution, pre-existing, not caused here.

AC-1..AC-11 of the closed nav-menu-elements-functional workstream: the map is a picker at all five levels in both designs; Tab / Enter / [ ] / - = / / stay bound; the prism follows the camera on WASD/R/F and the wheel; the drawn search reuses the whole existing search pipeline.

Hover resolves at the TAIL of the driver's render() — the legacy painters rewrite all three hover fields every frame from _mouseX/_mouseY against LEGACY geometry, so any new pointer state must be written there too or the legacy pass wins.
The legacy renderer keeps running underneath every mode frame ON PURPOSE — it is also the lazy loader (_renderLocal -> _ensureStarsLoaded; _renderSystem resolves _systemData).
_autopilotButtonRect is a live invisible button that _handleClick tests FIRST; any new interactive rect competes with that ordering.

A painter throw freezes the glass — PanelHost catches once, then stops uploading, and the screen keeps showing the last good frame and looks alive. Every new field the designs read needs a default in state.js.
S and D are MUTATED, never replaced — a fresh object leaves every design painting the frame the factory was built on, forever, and it repaints happily.
